references.text: The same command not to add anything or take anything away from God's commands is found here, which underscores the importance of preserving God's word unchanged.
It warns against adding anything to God's word, for then one will be found to be a liar. This reflects the same principle of not altering God's commands.
John warns against adding to or taking away from the words of this prophetic book, which is a direct parallel to the command in Deuteronomy.
The command to keep everything the Lord has commanded, without adding to it or taking anything away, is repeated here as an important exhortation to Israel.
Paul warns against preaching a different gospel than the one that was preached, reflecting the principle of not altering God's message.
Jesus confirms that he did not come to abolish the law but to fulfill it, and emphasizes the importance of keeping the commandments.
